if: goods are LOST, STOLEN, DESTROYED, WRITTEN OFF, or DISPOSED OF BY WAY OF GIFT OR FREE SAMPLES
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on those goods
note: Directly load-bearing for bookkeeping: a stock write-off, a shrinkage adjustment, a promotional free sample and a customer gift each trigger this clause, and credit already taken on those goods has to come out. The clause is drafted over goods only; it does not name services. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
